svg.title: A nurse is planning to implement relaxation strategies with a young child prior to a painful procedure. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
svg.desc: Relaxation in a young child is physical, not verbal : sit with them in a well-supported position such as against your chest, then rock or sway in long, wide, rhythmic movements . Bouncing is not the answer — fast, jerky motion stimulates rather than settles. Describing a pleasurable event is guided imagery , which needs enough language and imagination to be a school-age technique. Holding a breath and blowing it out is a breathing technique — and a toddler cannot reliably do it on command anyway. A note on that last one: most nursing sources file coached breathing under relaxation , while this question's rationale calls it distraction . Do not spend the question arguing the label — sort by what a child that age can actually do , and you land on the rocking either way.
